plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree covered in clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is among the most widely planted flowering cherries in temperate parks and along waterways.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in Japan's central regions and the mid-Atlantic United States; later in cooler northern areas
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The cherry blossom forecast is a national news event in Japan, and the trees planted around Washington D.C.'s Tidal Basin were a gift from Tokyo in 1912.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, and mid-April is peak display season in temperate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring, peaking in April in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Netherlands, Turkey, Central Asia origins; cultivated across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, a single rare bulb could cost more than a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: A low-growing annual or short-lived perennial with silky, cup-shaped flowers and feathery blue-green foliage. Flowers close at night and in cloudy weather, and open in full sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early spring to early summer, with spectacular 'superblooms' in April in wet years
plants.location: California, Oregon, and the southwestern United States; naturalized in Chile, Australia, and Europe
plants.funFact: It is the official state flower of California, and its blooms carpet entire hillsides like the Antelope Valley in spring.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large semi-deciduous tree producing masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers in panicles, with fern-like foliage. In the Southern Hemisphere it is mostly a spring bloomer, but in some tropical and subtropical areas flowering can occur at varied times.
plants.bloomingSeason: Tropical and subtropical regions flower variably from spring through early summer; some trees bloom in April in warm northern locations such as parts of India
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); cultivated in India, Africa, Australia, and the southern U.S.
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the tree is so abundant the city is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City'.
